page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance based on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance provides 12 vCPUs mapped across 6 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration comprises 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Memory sizing stands at 24.0 GB of RAM, establishing a compute-oriented 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction flags include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, and BMI2.

Hardware capabilities do not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating reliance on networked block storage volumes for persistent data. Network throughput is bounded by a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. The absence of local disk drives shifts primary data access latencies onto network I/O, which should be factored into disk-heavy pipeline architectures.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier performance across multi-threaded operations, contrasted with lower output in isolated single-threaded tasks. Multi-core evaluations such as stress-ng recorded 10,472.88, while Geekbench multi-core achieved 5,894.0. Conversely, single-thread processing yielded lower-quartile results, including a 1,310.99 stress-ng score and weak throughput in single-threaded gzip and bzip3 routines. Memory bandwidth remains balanced across uncached sweeps, logging 71.19 GB/sec in 256MB reads and 42.85 GB/sec in writes.

Given its balance of dedicated multi-core capacity and moderate memory, the instance delivers a practical resource allocation for compute-bound scaling. Cost efficiency is driven by providing high vCPU density without the overhead of surplus memory or dedicated accelerators. Suitable production workloads include web application serving, clustered container worker nodes, batch compilation, and distributed caching systems such as Redis.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.3xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 virtual instance configured with 12 vCPUs and 24.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with 6 physical cores and hyper-threading, it includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 instruction extensions. The instance includes no onboard local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage and a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate balanced multi-core and memory performance, registering average scores across multi-threaded stress-ng, Geekbench 6, and Redis benchmarks, while single-threaded tasks position in the lower performance quartile. The server is well aligned with compute-focused workloads, such as static web serving, Clang compilation, CI/CD pipeline workers, and distributed Redis caches that do not demand extensive memory footprints.
